answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds trust to an identity anchor and models topology as a trust graph. In a cut verification, auditor cliques inspect bridge bottlenecks isolating suspicious clusters. Should game-theoretic cross-auditing detect coordinated fraud, validators trigger stake slashing, bankrupting the adversary. This drives attacker cost to scale superlinearly, crashing fake swarm margins from their zenith like a fragile reef.
